blurb: A `\(…)` hole in a string takes a `String`, `Int`, `Float`, `Bool`, `Decimal`, `Instant`, `Duration`, or a refined type over one of them, and nothing else. An `Instant` prints as RFC 3339 UTC and a `Duration` as units, largest first (`1h30m`), the text their `toString()` gives. A record or sum has no canonical text, and Bynk will not print an unreadable stand-in such as `[object Object]`. An opaque type hides its base, so use `.raw` first. Turn other values into a `String` yourself: `toHex()` or `toBase64()` on `Bytes` (hex or base64 is a real choice), or interpolate the fields of a record, a `ValidationError` or a `DecodeError`.
summary: An interpolation hole holds a value with no string form.
